_README: Rich guide content for the SIM / eSIM / Wi-Fi plan page (English base). No invented prices (HARNESS): plans vary widely, so we compare by type and point to current offers. Rendered by components/SimGuide.jsx.

tldr: Solo & easiest: an eSIM — install it before you fly and it's live the moment you land.
No eSIM phone? A physical SIM from an airport counter (your phone must be unlocked).
Group or family: a rental pocket Wi-Fi is often cheapest shared — just return it before you fly home.
Don't quote a single price — compare by data amount and number of days.

highlights.title: eSIM is the easiest for most travelers
highlights.body: If your phone supports eSIM, buy one from an app (e.g. Airalo, Klook) before you fly, and your data is ready the instant you land — no counter, no SIM swap. Most Korea eSIMs run on the KT or SK Telecom network.

highlights.title: Pocket Wi-Fi wins for groups
highlights.body: A rental pocket Wi-Fi router shares one connection across several phones, so families and groups can split the daily cost. Pick it up at an airport kiosk — and remember to return it before your flight home.

highlights.title: A physical SIM needs an unlocked phone
highlights.body: Nano-SIMs from the airport carrier counters (SKT, KT, LG U+) only work in an unlocked phone. Bring your passport; setup takes about 10–15 minutes.

compare.title: eSIM vs physical SIM vs pocket Wi-Fi

rows.label: Get it
vals: Reserve online, pick up at kiosk

options.title: Set up your choice
options.intro: Pick the one that matches your phone and trip, then follow the quick setup.

cards.name: eSIM
setup: Buy a Korea eSIM in an app (Airalo, Klook, or a carrier) before you fly.
Install the eSIM following the app's QR/steps.
Turn on data roaming for that line when you land — you're online.

cards.name: Physical SIM
setup: Make sure your phone is unlocked.
Go to an SKT / KT / LG U+ counter in the arrivals hall (bring your passport).
Pick a plan by data + number of days.
Staff insert and activate it (~10–15 min).

cards.name: Pocket Wi-Fi
setup: Collect the router at the airport pickup kiosk.
Return it at the airport before you fly home.

items.d: A physical SIM won't work in a carrier-locked phone. Unlock it before you travel, or use an eSIM / pocket Wi-Fi instead.
Not every phone supports eSIM. Check your model first — otherwise plan for a physical SIM or pocket Wi-Fi.
Pocket Wi-Fi is a rental — return it at the airport before departure or you'll be charged.

items.t: Buying too much (or too little) data
items.d: Match the plan to your real use and trip length. Hotels and cafés have free Wi-Fi, so you may need less than you think.
For lots of national-park or coastal day trips, KT and SKT tend to have the widest coverage.

items.q: eSIM or physical SIM — which should I get?
items.a: If your phone supports eSIM, get an eSIM: install it before you fly and it works the moment you land. If not (or you prefer a physical card), buy a SIM at an airport counter — your phone must be unlocked.

items.q: What's best for a family or group?
items.a: A rental pocket Wi-Fi is usually cheapest when several people share one router. Just remember to return it at the airport before flying home.

items.q: Where do I buy at the airport?
items.a: All three carriers (SKT, KT, LG U+) have counters in the arrivals halls at Incheon (Terminals 1 & 2), Gimpo and Gimhae. You can also pre-order online.

Plans vary widely by data amount and number of days, so we don't quote a single price — compare current offers in an eSIM app or at the counters. Do check the data and validity, not just the headline price.

items.q: Do I even need one — isn't there free Wi-Fi?
items.a: There's lots of free Wi-Fi (airport, hotels, cafés, some buses/subway), but your own data makes maps, taxis and messaging reliable on the move. Most visitors get an eSIM or SIM.
